document: Ofcom Broadcasting Code, Section One: Protecting the Under-Eighteens
scope / applicability: All Ofcom-licensed TV and radio. Rules 1.3-1.6 do NOT apply to BBC ODPS.
notes: The core UK rulebook. Must be read with Section Two.

document: Ofcom Broadcasting Code, Section Two: Harm and Offence
scope / applicability: Same as UK-S1.
notes: Supplies the BINDING DEFINITION OF 'CONTEXT', on which Section One depends. Time of broadcast is one of its eight factors.

document: Ofcom Guidance: Protecting the Under-Eighteens - Observing the watershed on television and music videos
scope / applicability: Television.
notes: The ONLY UK source with operational detail on MUSIC VIDEOS and on the post-watershed ramp.

document: Ofcom Guidance Notes, Section One
scope / applicability: Interpretation aid for S1.
notes: IDENTIFIED BUT NOT EXTRACTED in v1. Would sharpen the judgment_based thresholds.

document: Ofcom Guidance Notes, Section Two
scope / applicability: Interpretation aid for S2.
notes: IDENTIFIED BUT NOT EXTRACTED in v1.

document: Ofcom Statement: Review of the mandatory daytime protection rules
scope / applicability: Premium subscription film, pay-per-view, and from 2019-01-01 scheduled channels on vertically integrated pay-TV platforms. NOT free-to-air DTT.
notes: Created the MDP regime and amended Rules 1.23-1.25. The clearest UK proof that rating does not determine hours.

document: Ofcom Broadcast and On Demand Bulletins (enforcement decisions)
scope / applicability: Applied thresholds.
notes: Example: Toofan, NTV, 2026-05-29 11:30 - violent film not appropriately scheduled, breach of Rule 1.3. The only source of APPLIED thresholds for judgment_based rules; should be ingested systematically.

document: Communications Act 2003, ss. 3(4)(h), 319(2)(a) & (f)
scope / applicability: Legal basis for Ofcom's standards duty.
notes: s.319(2)(a): 'that persons under the age of eighteen are protected'.

document: The Audiovisual Media Services Regulations 2020 (SI 2020/1062)
scope / applicability: Implemented revised AVMSD duties into UK law post-Brexit.
notes: Confirms content standards for broadcast TV remain in the Ofcom Code.

document: BBFC classification
scope / applicability: Film classification. NOT a TV regulator.
notes: In scope only as an INPUT: the Ofcom Code refers to BBFC ratings in Rules 1.17, 1.22, 1.23, 1.24, 1.25, 1.26.

document: Recommandation n. 2005-5 du 7 juin 2005 (signaletique jeunesse et classification des programmes), as amended
scope / applicability: Editors of linear TV services in France; all conventionnees et declarees channels.
date / version: JORF n.158, 2005-07-08, text n.92; amended 2012 and 2014
notes: THE CORE FRENCH FRAMEWORK. Art. 2 defines categories I-V; art. 3 sets programming conditions.

document: Deliberation n. 2012-57 du 23 octobre 2012 modifying FR-R1
scope / applicability: Amended art. 4(2)(a) - category II on-screen signage.

document: Deliberation n. 2014-17 du 5 mars 2014 modifying FR-R1
scope / applicability: Replaced arts. 1, 3, 4; amended art. 2; inserted a new art. 5 (trailers and music videos).
notes: THE CURRENT OPERATIVE TEXT for French scheduling. The Arcom English page is a DeepL machine translation and is garbled at art. 3 (C-02).

document: Recommandation n. 2004-7 du 15 decembre 2004 - category V programmes
scope / applicability: Editors AND distributors broadcasting category V (-18), mainland France and overseas departements.
notes: THE SOLE SOURCE of the French -18 hours (00:00-05:00). Art. 3 of FR-R1 defers to it entirely. Upheld by Conseil d'Etat 2006-05-17, nos. 263081/277711. CURRENCY UNCONFIRMED (C-03).

document: Recommandation du 26 juillet 2005 - category V, overseas France
scope / applicability: Overseas departements.
notes: Noted, NOT extracted in v1.

document: Arcom youth-signage public awareness page
scope / applicability: Plain-language per-category meanings and broadcast times.
notes: UNRELIABLE for -12: describes it with the same wording as -10 ('during the day, under certain conditions'), contradicting the binding text (C-01). Useful corroboration for -16 ('as of 10:30 pm') and -18 ('between midnight and 5 a.m.').

document: Loi n. 86-1067 du 30 septembre 1986, arts. 1 and 15
scope / applicability: All French audiovisual communication services.
notes: Art. 15 is the statutory duty and establishes the TWO-TIER HARM STANDARD: 'nuire gravement' = absolute prohibition; 'nuire' = permitted if broadcast time and/or technical means keep minors away.

document: Channel conventions (per-channel agreements with Arcom)
scope / applicability: CHANNEL-SPECIFIC. Can be stricter than the general recommendation.
notes: NOT COLLECTED in v1 (C-06). Example: the C8 mise en demeure cites convention arts. 2-3-7, 2-4, 4-2-1 alongside reco. 2005-5. For Task 2: a per-licensee source that cannot be scraped generically.

document: CNC / Commission de classification des oeuvres cinematographiques (visa d'exploitation)
scope / applicability: CINEMA RELEASES ONLY. The CNC states its commission is competent neither for television, DVD, VOD, video games nor the internet.
notes: OUT OF SCOPE as a rule source; IN SCOPE as an optional input for theatrical films. A cinema interdiction pulls a film into at least the matching TV category; a CNC 'avertissement' maps to -12 for TV.

document: solidarites.gouv.fr - Classification et signaletique de la television
scope / applicability: Government summary of the signaletique regime.
notes: USED TO DISAMBIGUATE the garbled Arcom English translation of art. 3 (C-02). States plainly: non-cinema channels not before 22h for -12; cinema channels not Wednesdays before 20h30; -16 after 22h30 / 20h30.

document: Deliberation n. 2011-64 du 20 decembre 2011 - protection of minors, ON-DEMAND (SMAD) services
scope / applicability: NON-LINEAR services established in France.
notes: OUT OF SCOPE (non-linear) but a VALUABLE CONTRAST: reuses the same five categories with DIFFERENT conditions (e.g. category IV not behind payment is accessible only 22:30-05:00). Proves the same category maps to different hours on different service types.

document: AVMSD - Directive 2010/13/EU as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/1808, Article 6a
scope / applicability: Binds Member States, NOT directly applicable to a broadcast.
notes: The common ancestor of both national frameworks. Mandates an OUTCOME and permits time, age verification or other technical measures as ALTERNATIVES - the root cause of the rating-vs-hours asymmetry.

document: European Audiovisual Observatory - protection of minors / AVMSD spotlight
scope / applicability: Comparative mapping across Member States.
notes: Useful starting point for Task 2 scaling to dozens of countries.
